subject: Request for normalization of rolling latency metric after partial BGP flap
messages:
From: Northern SRE <ops@northernhealth.org>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-27T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Rolling-3m latency spike on 2026-12-25 — request for normalization

Hi Tessa,

We dug into a recurring alert from our end for the 2026-12-25 03:14–06:22 UTC window. Our synthetic checks show sustained p95 increases (from ~210ms to ~1.2s) for ~2.5 hours; the 3-minute rolling uptime calculation on our side marks that as a partial degradation. We looked at your public status and the uptime ledger, and the system counted the full window toward availability.

We believe the root cause is a transient BGP flap reported by our transit partner (their ticket attached) that only impacted a subset of POPs handling ~13% of our traffic. Given that this was an upstream peer event and not a global Redwood fleet degradation, could you please:

- Confirm whether Redwood will exclude the impacted POPs/paths from the rolling-window normalization, or apply a traffic-weighted normalization?
- Share the telemetry you used to compute the rolling-window uptime for our account for that window (we attached our sample SLO calc and synthetic charts).

Attachments: nh_latency_chart.png (2x png), slo_calc.csv (sample data)

We would like a decision on whether this window will count toward the monthly uptime calculation and any proposed credits.

Thanks,
Alex G.
Northern Health — SRE
ops@northernhealth.org

---

On Sun, 2026-12-25 at 07:40 UTC our monitoring flagged the increase; we saved traces and can share link to traces on request.

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Alex G. <ops@northernhealth.org>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-27T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Rolling-3m latency spike on 2026-12-25 — request for normalization

Alex — thanks for the detailed notes and the artifacts. We're looking into this now. A couple quick clarifying Qs while we pull telemetry:

1) Do you have a breakdown by DC/POP for the synthetic failures (so we can map traffic fraction to POPs)?
2) Can you confirm whether any application-layer errors (5xx) accompanied the latency spike, or was it purely increased latency?

Ben, Marissa — looping you in. Ben can you pull the per-pop request counts and our internal routing logs between 03:00–07:00 UTC on 2026-12-25. Rishi, tagging you for any routing/BGP evidence we have in our telemetry. Laura, FYI in case legal needs to review any SLA language for exclusions.

We aim to come back with a proposed normalization approach by EOD PST tomorrow.

—Tessa

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-27T12:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Rolling-3m latency spike on 2026-12-25 — request for normalization

Tessa / Alex — I pulled our per-POP request logs and here's a short summary:

- Between 03:10–06:20 UTC we see a ~11–15% drop in requests served from three POPs (us-west-1-edge, us-west-2-edge, us-west-3-edge).
- P95 latency for requests that were routed through alternate POPs remained within normal bounds (~220–260ms).
- Error rate did not spike significantly (5xx remained <0.1%); most customers experienced higher latency rather than errors.

We reached out to the upstream provider to confirm a BGP flap. Attaching their log extract (peerswitch_bgp_log.txt). Per our initial read, this looks like a partial-path issue — not a Redwood control-plane or global runtime failure.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- If we apply an exclusion, it should be limited to the affected POPs and normalized by the fraction of traffic they handled for Northern Health (we can compute that precisely).
- If we do not exclude, the rolling-window metric will count the full window (standard calculation).

Attaching: peerswitch_bgp_log.txt (excerpt)

Ben Carter
Support Lead — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: PeerSwitch NOC <bgp-support@peerswitch.net>
To: Support <ben.carter@redwood.com>, tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-27T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Incident — BGP flap — 2026-12-25 03:00–06:30 UTC

Hi Ben / Redwood team,

We saw a transient BGP adjacency reset across three of our west-coast POPs starting 2026-12-25T03:08:14Z and stabilizing by 2026-12-25T06:20:09Z. The flap affected a subset of our peering sessions to some downstream CDNs and resulted in path churn; traffic that had egress affinity to those sessions experienced latency increases while traffic re-converged.

We are attaching the BGP log extract and RIB diffs. This was not a Redwood control-plane change. Per our SLA with providers, and typical cloud/edge practices, customers will sometimes see partial-path latency when a peer has a flap.

Attachment: peerswitch_bgp_log.txt

Regards,
PeerSwitch NOC
bgp-support@peerswitch.net

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: alex.g@northhealth.org, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-27T15:40:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Incident — BGP flap — proposed normalization approach

Folks — forwarding the vendor confirmation (quoted below) and the Northern Health artifacts. Summary: vendor confirms BGP flap that hit three POPs and caused path re-convergence; our logs show ~13% of NH traffic was impacted and primarily experienced latency (not errors).

I propose the following for decision:

1) Apply a traffic-weighted normalization for that window by excluding the affected POPs and recalculating the rolling-window uptime for Northern Health using (total_successful_requests_from_unaffected_POPs)/(total_requests). This mirrors the partial-path normalization approach we used in earlier edge incidents.

2) As a customer-facing item, offer a one-time goodwill credit equivalent to 5% of December usage for the inconvenience (we can convert to actual $ once finance confirms).

Notes/attachments: SLA_section_uptime.pdf (excerpt of exclusion language), calc_proposal.xlsx (proposal showing how to compute weighted uptime), peerswitch_bgp_log.txt, nh_latency_chart.png

Please advise if anyone objects to (1) or (2) or prefers a different apportionment. I need a sign-off to communicate to Northern Health and to execute the adjustment in the uptime ledger.

—Tessa
Account Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.com, alex.g@northhealth.org
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-28T16:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Incident — BGP flap — proposed normalization approach

Thanks everyone for the investigation and the clear artifacts. Rishi and I reviewed the telemetry and vendor logs. Our view:

- This was a third-party path issue that affected a discrete subset of POPs and approximately 12.8% of Northern Health's traffic. It does not meet our internal threshold for a full-service outage exclusion.
- However, excluding the impacted POPs and recalculating by traffic-weight (the math in calc_proposal.xlsx) is reasonable and consistent with precedent.

Decision: Proceed with traffic-weighted normalization for the 2026-12-25 03:08–06:20 UTC window. We will:

1) Recompute the rolling-window uptime for Northern Health excluding the affected POPs for that window and update the uptime ledger.
2) Apply a one-time goodwill credit equal to 5% of December usage (finance will compute the dollar amount; Ben, please coordinate).
3) Add an internal note to the account record that this normalization was approved under the third-party partial-path exception.

Ben — please run the recalculation and add the ledger entry. Laura — no further legal action needed here; keep on file. Tessa — please communicate the decision and credit offer to Northern Health, include the calculation detail and the updated ledger entries once complete.

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
